plain_english_policy: Enactment would allow first-time felony offenders convicted of capital murder who have served at least 20 years without parole to petition for a sentence reduction from life without the possibility of parole (LWOP) to life with the possibility of parole, provided they meet specific behavioral and disciplinary requirements during their incarceration. The policy creates a new legal mechanism (§13A-5-57.1) enabling judicial review after 20 years if the offender has no prior felonies, no record of assault on inmates or staff in the preceding 10 years, no escape attempts in the preceding 10 years, no sexual assaults in the preceding 10 years, and no drug/alcohol violations (via positive urine tests) in the preceding 5 years. If granted, the sentence becomes life with parole eligibility; if denied, petitioners may reapply every two years. The law applies retroactively to those already serving LWOP sentences as of its effective date.
policy_direction_if_enacted: The policy direction is a conditional relaxation of mandatory minimum sentencing for capital murder cases involving first-time offenders who demonstrate long-term institutional compliance and rehabilitation over 20+ years, introducing judicial discretion in sentence reduction while maintaining strict behavioral thresholds to prevent abuse or reward violent recidivists.
sponsorship_supports_position: Representatives Fields and McAdory affirmatively advanced this bill, indicating support for expanding post-incarceration relief mechanisms under strict conditions.
evidence_quotes: the offender may petition a sentencing court for reconsideration of the life imprisonment without the possibility of parole sentence to be reduced to a sentence of life with the possibility of parole after the offender has served 20 years on his or her life without parole sentence.
